D.t: Lynne Walz trails by 4.5 and wins 19% of simulations. Closing it takes about 17,634 voters switching sides, or 35,269 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +11.1 and D +2.1. A normal polling error decides it.

The polls page average is R +3.3. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners for Education Reform Now Advocacy (D) at D +0.3; your worst is National Public Affairs at R +5.1. 7 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Douglas, a projected net 65,360 votes; Lancaster, a projected net 32,742 votes; Sarpy, a projected net 6,166 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Lynne Walz runs furthest behind in Platte, Madison, Washington. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 90% of voters, 42 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.48 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 69% of voters, 43 to 50, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.46 points; Voters without a degree, 60% of voters, 41 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.00 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Lynne Walz: Immigration voters 17 to 76, Small counties 26 to 67, Voters who can afford daily costs 34 to 59. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$860K cash against $7.5M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
